title: U.S. stock futures dip after high yields batter tech; Trump-Xi summit begins
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com-- U.S. stock index futures fell slightly on Wednesday evening as a rebound in Treasury yields battered technology stocks, with focus squarely on upcoming talks between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
S&P 500 Futures fell 0.1% to 7,765.0 points by 21:02 ET (01:02 GMT). Nasdaq 100 Futures fell 0.1% to 30,737.75 points, while Dow Jones Futures fell 0.13% to 51,803.0 points.
Futures steadied after a negative session on Wall Street, as a spike in Treasury yields, following strong economic data, rattled equity markets. High-flying technology stocks were especially hit by surging yields.
Markets were also spooked by a sharp rebound in oil prices, as recent hopes for U.S.-Iran diplomacy appeared largely overstated, with a standoff in the Strait of Hormuz showing few signs of lifting.
China’s Xi lands in Washington with bilateral talks on tap
Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Washington on Wednesday evening, where he was met by Trump.
The two will engage in bilateral talks on Thursday, with artificial intelligence and trade expected to be at the top of the agenda.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of the summit, and told Fox News on Wednesday that Washington and Beijing had agreed to extend their trade truce by two months to early-January.
On the AI front, markets will be watching whether Trump and Xi align on growing demands for more AI safety regulations. Discussions over more AI chip sales to China will also be in close focus.
Markets will also be watching for more cues on China’s rare earth exports and its commitment to purchasing more U.S. agricultural exports.
Wall St battered by yield spike, Iran tensions
Wall Street indexes fell on Wednesday, with the NASDAQ Composite leading losses in a 1.1% slide from record highs hit earlier in the week.
Markets were battered by a spike in Treasury yields after stronger than expected purchasing managers index data highlighted strength in the U.S. economy and pushed up concerns over more interest rate hikes.
The benchmark 10-year yield soared past 5% and briefly hit its highest level since 2007. Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr also underpinned yields.
A rebound in oil prices also dented Wall Street after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian struck a defiant tone in an address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Separately, reports said the U.S. had rejected Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. officials also downplayed recent dialogue with Iran.

title: U.S., China agree to extend trade truce until January, Bessent says
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com-- The United States and China have agreed to extend their "Busan agreement" trade truce until Jan. 10, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday, providing more time for the two countries to work toward a broader economic deal.
Bessent made the announcement after meeting Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in Washington, ahead of a summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
"We have agreed today that we will extend what we call the Busan Agreement," Bessent said in an interview with Fox News, adding that the arrangement, originally due to expire on Nov. 10, would be extended to Jan. 10.
The truce, reached at a Trump-Xi meeting in Busan, South Korea, last year, lowered tariffs that had surged during a period of tit-for-tat trade measures. China also agreed to ease restrictions on rare earth magnets and other critical minerals.
Bessent said earlier on Wednesday that Washington was open to either extending the existing arrangement or pursuing a larger trade deal proposed by Beijing.
The extension comes as the two sides continue talks on trade, artificial intelligence and critical minerals ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.

title: Oil slips 1% after sharp gains amid U.S.-Iran diplomacy doubts
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com-- Oil prices slipped in Asian trading Thursday after jumping nearly 4% in the previous session, as investors weighed renewed tensions between Washington and Tehran against signs that diplomatic efforts to end the conflict remained possible.
As of 20:32 ET (00:32 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in November fell 1% to $102.10 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 0.7% to $91.50 per barrel.
Brent crude futures settled nearly 4% higher on Wednesday, while WTI crude climbed nearly 2%.
Get premium commodity market insights with InvestigPro -- at 50% off now
The rally followed Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s address to the United Nations General Assembly, in which he said Iran would not surrender to U.S. pressure while maintaining that Tehran remained open to diplomacy.
His comments came a day after U.S. President Donald Trump warned he could "annihilate" Iran if a deal to end the conflict could not be reached.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran was reviewing Washington’s response to an Iranian proposal to end hostilities, although significant differences remained. Indirect discussions have included the possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the lifting of a U.S. naval blockade on Iran.
The Strait remains a key focus for oil markets because it normally handles roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas shipments.
Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Wednesday that the waterway would not reopen until Tehran’s conditions were met.
At the same time, improving Gulf supply has limited the upside in crude. Saudi Arabia has restarted operations on its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, while Iraq has increased exports and expects to raise shipments through Turkey.
U.S. diesel was another focus after a report that the White House was considering a 90-day ban on diesel exports sent U.S. ultra-low-sulfur diesel futures sharply lower on Wednesday. The White House later dismissed the report as "fake news."
U.S. crude inventories also rose by 3 million barrels to 426.4 million barrels in the week ended Sept. 18, according to the Energy Information Administration, compared with analysts’ expectations for a 640,000-barrel draw.
Gasoline inventories fell by 1.7 million barrels, while distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, declined by 400,000 barrels.
The data are particularly relevant for the diesel market, where supplies remain under pressure even as crude stocks have increased.

title: Meta debuts new handheld device dedicated to using Muse
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com-- Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META) on Wednesday unveiled a new palm-sized device dedicated to running its Muse artificial intelligence agent, along with more models of its popular smart glasses, including a camera-less version.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled the new products when delivering the opening keynote at the Meta Connect 2026 event in Menlo Park, California.
The handheld device, called Muse Charm, features a small screen and 5G connectivity, allowing users to interact with their Muse agents without using their phone. The device will be available to purchase by December.
Get more breaking news on the biggest AI stocks by subscribing to InvestingPro
Zuckerberg unveiled the device amid a host of new product reveals, including a new pair of camera-less smart glasses, virtual reality glasses, and more plans for the company’s popular Muse agents.
The Meta CEO said Muse could generate financial returns for users, and that Meta was leaning into this feature by making Muse free for a “huge number of tokens,” with plans to charge a “small” transaction fee.
“In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people are going to use,” Zuckerberg said.
Zuckerberg unveiled more personalization options for Muse, with users able to alter their AI agent’s appearance and voice. He also said Muse will be tightly integrated into Meta’s AI smart glasses.
Meta Chief AI Officer Alexander Wang said the company was adding more capabilities to Muse, now allowing the agent to directly interact with a user’s computer.
Wang also touted “connectors,” which allow Muse to integrate with partner applications. Wang said ecommerce, specifically agentic shopping, was a major feature of the AI product.
Wang announced Muse integration with more retailers, including Walmart and Best Buy.
Meta released Muse as a phone application in early-September to rapidly growing popularity. It recently overtook OpenAI’s ChatGPT to become the most downloaded app on Apple’s U.S. App Store.
Muse’s popularity sparked a rally across AI stocks amid hopes that growing consumer adoption of AI will boost overall demand for the technology.
Meta’s shares trimmed aftermarket losses to trade down 0.4% by 20:40 ET (00:40 GMT). They had earlier fallen as much as 1.5%.

title: Gold steadies after selloff as oil, strong U.S. data lift Fed hike bets
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com -- Gold prices were little changed on Thursday after a sharp selloff in the previous session, as higher oil prices and stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data kept expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes elevated.
At 20:08 ET (00:08 GMT), XAU/USD rose 0.2% to $4,295.5 an ounce, while XAG/USD fell 0.2% to $64.31. The U.S. dollar index was little changed after rising for four straight sessions to a near two-month high. Higher Treasury yields and a firm dollar added to the pressure on bullion.
Oil rises as Iran tensions cloud peace prospects
Gold has remained highly sensitive to the outlook for Fed policy as investors assess whether higher energy prices will keep inflation elevated enough to require further rate increases. Higher rates tend to weigh on gold because the metal pays no interest.
Oil prices rose after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the United Nations that Iran would not allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a U.S. blockade remain in place.
His comments underscored the difficulty of reaching a peace agreement with Washington despite renewed diplomatic efforts this week.
Pezeshkian said Iran remains willing to negotiate but will not respond to threats. He also said Tehran does not seek to build a nuclear weapon, while insisting it will not surrender its right to develop nuclear technology for economic purposes.
This comes a day after President Donald Trump said U.S. officials had “very good” talks with Iranian envoys on the sidelines of the United Nations summit.
Gold has fallen roughly 20% since the U.S.-Iran war began in late February, with energy prices and the Fed outlook remaining major drivers.
Strong U.S. data, Treasury selloff reinforce rate pressure
The U.S. Treasury market came under renewed pressure after stronger-than-expected economic data and a weak debt auction. The moves reflected growing expectations that inflation will remain sticky, with yields across most maturities reaching their highest levels in almost two decades.
The five-year U.S. Treasury yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2007, adding another headwind for non-yielding bullion.
U.S. business activity also expanded at its fastest pace in more than five years. Fed Governor Michael Barr said further rate increases are likely needed to bring inflation back to the central bank's 2% target. His comments followed similar warnings from other policymakers that price pressures remain persistent.
Swap markets are now pricing at least three Fed rate hikes by April next year, up from earlier this week.
Despite the near-term pressure, gold remains supported by longer-term demand considerations. For now, however, stronger economic activity, higher yields, rising oil prices and a firmer dollar are keeping the metal under pressure.

title: Australia jobs beat forecasts in Aug, but unemployment hits 5-yr high
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com-- Australia’s labour market showed mixed signs in August, with employment growth exceeding expectations but the unemployment rate rising to a five-year high as more people entered the labour force.
Employment rose by 39,500 in August, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday, compared with a 21,500 increase expected by economists and a 15,900 decline in July.
The increase was driven by a 45,600 rise in part-time employment, while full-time employment fell by 6,300.
The unemployment rate rose to 4.6% from 4.5%, compared with economists’ expectations for it to remain at 4.5%. The reading was the highest since November 2021.
The number of unemployed people increased by about 28,000 during the month.
ABS head of labour statistics Sean Crick said a higher proportion of people who had previously been outside the labour force moved into unemployment in August than in recent years.
The participation rate rose to 67.1% from 66.9%, matching its highest level on record, as a larger share of people joined the labour force.
Hours worked rose 0.7% in August, after falling by the same amount in July.
The figures come ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia’s Sept. 29 policy decision. The central bank has raised its cash rate by 75 basis points this year to 4.35%, where it was held in August.
Earlier this week, RBA Governor Michele Bullock said that unemployment may need to rise into a 4.5%-5% range to help restrain inflation, while Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said another rate increase may be needed.
Markets were pricing a high probability of a hike at next week’s meeting.

The 10-year rate jumped 2.5% to 3.058%, reaching its highest level since August 1996. This came after the U.S. 10-year rate hit a 19-year high in overnight trade, crossing the closely watched 5% mark.

Japanese PMI data released earlier on Thursday also showed business activity continuing to grow. This came less than a week after the Bank of Japan hiked interest rates to a 30-year high, and signaled more potential hikes to calm sticky inflation.
An overnight surge in oil prices also added to concerns over rising inflation and its effects on monetary policy, while a spike in the dollar pressured the yen.

title: European shares slip as US-Iran talks shows little progress
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com - European equities slipped on Thursday, surrendering early stability as a diplomatic impasse between Washington and Tehran, tech sector warnings over artificial intelligence risks, and rising sovereign bond yields sapped market conviction.
The STOXX 600 index fell 0.4%. Germany’s DAX and France’s CAC 40 slipped 0.6% and 0.4% respectively. London’s FTSE 100 fell 0.3%
Middle east peace deadlock
Expectations of an immediate diplomatic breakthrough at the United Nations General Assembly faded as U.S. and Iranian officials remained far apart on terms for a formal peace agreement and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, reigniting energy risk premia.
Sentiment in growth listings took a hit after global technology leaders voiced growing concern over near-term artificial intelligence deployment risks, monetisation timelines, and regulatory hurdles ahead of high-level tech panels in Washington.
Investors held elevated cash buffers as Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump prepared for high-stakes bilateral talks in Washington later in the day, with markets eyeing prospective progress on trade relations and technology export protocols.
"Expectations for the Trump-Xi summit are modest, but that doesn’t mean it lacks significance. From rare earth minerals and tariffs to AI and the conflict in the Middle East, this meeting carries real implications for the global economy," said Lukman Otunuga, head of market research at FXTM.
French assets remained in focus as markets braced for fresh French business climate and consumer confidence survey data due later in the session.
The upcoming economic indicators arrive against a grim fiscal backdrop where the cost of insuring French government debt against default via credit default swaps (CDS) has touched multi-year highs.
Investors continue to demand a significant risk premium to hold French OATs, leaving French sovereign bonds among the worst performers in the euro area as parliamentary gridlock obscures the path toward structural budget consolidation.
US yields surge
Adding to the global equity drag, U.S. Treasury yields climbed to multi-year highs overnight as fixed-income traders aggressively priced in the likelihood of synchronized central bank tightening.
According to the CME FedWatch tool, money markets are now discounting a 70% probability, up from 50% of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month.
The surge in global risk-free rates continues to put severe pressure on equity multiples, threatening to snap the STOXX 600’s multi-month winning streak as elevated borrowing costs, volatile gas prices, and hawkish central bank guidance test investor conviction.

title: Judge orders Trump to restore White House media access to banned outlets
full_text:
Investing.com-- A federal judge ruled Thursday that President Donald Trump must temporarily restore White House access for journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico, stating that the ban on these three media outlets was unconstitutional.
U.S. District Judge Tim Kelly issued the order in a lawsuit filed by the news organizations challenging the Trump’s September 18 ban.
Kelly ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets’ press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days. The judge rejected the government’s claim that the ban was motivated by national security concerns.
Trump had accused the three outlets of constantly reporting "FICTION and LIES," while Justice Department lawyers had attempted to justify the ban on national security grounds.
In response, the three outlets sued Trump and his administration in federal court in Washington on Monday. Several other media outlets, including Fox News, had also boycotted the White House in protest against Trump’s ban.

title: Vistry shares fall 8% after wider-than-expected H1 loss
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com -- Vistry Group shares fell on Thursday after the housebuilder reported a larger-than-expected first-half loss, as discounts on Open Market homes to generate cash and costs linked to its strategic review weighed on earnings.
Vistry shares fell 8.21% to 246.97 pence, touching their lowest level since July 10 and significantly underperforming the FTSE 250, which was down 0.7%
Vistry reported a loss attributable of £607 million, compared with a consensus loss of about £30.8 million in the supplied pre-earnings estimates.
Revenue fell to £1.42 billion, below consensus of about £1.47 billion, while adjusted profit before tax swung to a £83.3 million loss, versus an expected loss of about £30.1 million.
Vistry now expects its year-end cash position to be broadly neutral, below its previous expectation of more than £100 million of net cash, after weaker private-home sales and the renegotiation or withdrawal of some partner deals.
The company expects around £165 million of adjusted profit before tax excluding about £470 million of strategic items, while a further £40 million reduction to year-end profit reflects partner deals being pushed out as they are renegotiated.
It expects adjusted PBT of about £185 million in FY27, assuming broadly stable market conditions.
The group also identified £50 million a year of additional overhead savings, on top of £25 million previously identified, with management targeting materially lower leverage over the coming years.
The company said Vistry does not anticipate needing to raise equity and expects the new strategy to support stronger cash-backed earnings and returns.

title: Asian currencies mixed as dollar holds two-month high, yen stays near lows
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com -- Asian currencies traded mixed on Thursday, while the U.S. dollar held near a two-month high as stronger U.S. economic data revived inflation concerns and boosted rate-hike bets.
The Japanese yen steadied near a three-week low after Japan returned from holidays, while South Korean markets were closed for the Chuseok holiday.
The U.S. dollar index was around 101.09, after touching 101.2 earlier. The USD/JPY pair fell 0.2% to 157.94, leaving the yen close to its weakest level in three weeks.
The dollar's gains followed a stronger-than-expected U.S. manufacturing reading that revived concerns about inflation. A poorly received $70 billion five-year Treasury auction then triggered another round of selling across the bond market, pushing the five-year yield above 5% for the first time since 2007.
Dollar gains as Fed bets strengthen on inflation risks
Fed Governor Michael Barr said a strong economy and rising inflation risks could require further rate hikes, boosting bets on an October increase.
CME FedWatch pricing now implies almost a 70% chance of an October increase, up from about 50% a week ago.
Oil has added to the inflation pressure. Brent crude settled around $103 a barrel after rising almost 4% on Wednesday. The move followed Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's pledge that Tehran would not surrender, while markets also assessed U.S. efforts to restrict diesel exports.
Iran has also said it would not allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while U.S. sanctions and a naval blockade remain in place, adding to uncertainty around energy supplies.
Yen stays weak as Japan returns from holiday
Japan's markets reopened Thursday after a holiday, with the 10-year Japanese government bond yield rising to around 3.06%, its highest level in three decades.
The yen remained under pressure despite the jump in Japanese yields, as markets continued to assess whether the BOJ's recent rate increase was sufficiently hawkish.
The USD/JPY pair was around 157.94. Traders remain alert to possible intervention after the BOJ raised rates to a 31-year high last week, but markets judged the decision as lacking a strong enough signal on further tightening.
Separately, Japan's flash manufacturing PMI fell to 54.1 in September from 54.9 in August.
Won, rupiah weaken as markets watch oil and policy
The South Korean won weakened in the latest FX pricing, with the USD/KRW pair up 0.5% at 1,372.1. South Korean stock markets were closed Thursday for Chuseok and will remain shut Friday, limiting domestic market signals.
The Australian dollar was around $0.70, while the New Zealand dollar was at $0.57. The USD/AUD pair rose 0.1%. The USD/SGD pair rose marginally to 1.2801.
The Indonesian rupiah was among the weaker regional currencies, with the USD/IDR pair rising 0.6% to 17,903.5. Bank Indonesia kept its benchmark rate at 5.75% on Wednesday, as expected, while saying it would continue using exchange-rate stabilization measures and incentives for foreign inflows.
Rupee, yuan stay in focus as China talks loom
The Indian rupee was slightly firmer, with the USD/INR pair down 0.02% at 95.915. The RBI has also been draining surplus banking liquidity through bond sales and foreign-exchange swaps, limiting the risk that excess cash could add to inflation pressure.
The Chinese yuan remained under some pressure after its recent rally. The USD/CNH pair rose 0.1% to 6.72, while USD/CNY gained 0.1% to 6.71. The yuan had earlier strengthened through the 6.70 level to more than a 3-1/2-year high.
The yuan's next moves are closely linked to the upcoming meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The current trade truce is expected to be extended for another two months, but negotiations over artificial intelligence, rare-earth exports, U.S. aircraft purchases and agricultural goods remain unresolved.

title: Europe EV sales rose in August as petrol, diesel demand fades; Stellantis falls
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
Investing.com -- Demand for electrified vehicles continued to drive growth in Europe’s car market in August, offsetting a steep decline in petrol and diesel sales, according to data released Thursday by the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association.
Shares in Stellantis, which retains heavy exposure to combustion-engine models, fell 1.4% after the report by 07:29 GMT.
New EU car registrations rose 5.3% year-to-date through August, even as rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty weighed on the broader economy. Battery-electric cars captured 21.7% of the EU market, up from 15.8% a year earlier, with 1,641,333 units registered in the first eight months of the year.
Growth was led by France, up 74.2%, Germany, up 53.1%, and Denmark, up 40.9%, three of the EU’s four largest markets, together accounting for 64% of all battery-electric registrations.
Hybrid-electric vehicles remained the most popular choice among EU consumers, with a 36.6% market share and 2,759,718 units registered, supported by gains in Spain, up 21%, and Italy, up 20.5%. Plug-in hybrids also gained ground, rising to a 10% market share from 8.8% a year earlier, with 758,082 units registered, driven by strong growth in Italy, Spain and Germany.
Petrol and diesel cars continued to lose ground. Petrol registrations fell 18.6%, with France posting the steepest drop at 35.8%, while diesel registrations also declined 18.6%. Combined, petrol and diesel models’ market share fell to 29% from 37.5% a year earlier.
The data also showed Chinese automakers continuing to expand their presence across the EU, U.K. and European Free Trade Association markets.

Investing.com-- Bitcoin fell on Thursday, extending steep overnight losses as a spike in oil prices and Treasury yields ramped up concerns over higher interest rates.
Broader cryptocurrency prices also fell, as a fall in risk appetite spurred some profit-taking after stellar gains in the sector through September.
Bitcoin fell 2.7% to $84,148.7 by 02:14 ET (06:14 GMT).
But the world’s largest crypto was still sitting on strong gains so far in September, as investors welcomed more regulatory favor from the U.S. government.

Bitcoin sinks as Treasury yields hit 19-yr high, oil rebounds
Bitcoin’s overnight losses came in tandem with broader risk-driven markets, which fell amid a sharp surge in Treasury yields.
The U.S. 10-year benchmark jumped back above 5% and to its strongest level since 2007, as robust U.S. purchasing managers index data and hawkish comments from a Federal Reserve Governor ramped up bets on more rate hikes in the coming months.
The Fed raised rates by 25 basis points last week and reiterated its commitment to a 2% annual inflation target, which markets interpreted as heralding more rate hikes.
Bond yields surged across the developed world on expectations of more rate hikes. Japanese 10-year yields hit a 30-year high on Thursday.
Higher rates diminish the appeal of risky, speculative investments like Bitcoin, given that debt usually offers better returns in such environments.
Adding to concerns over higher rates, oil prices rebounded overnight as bets on more U.S.-Iran diplomacy appeared to be overstated.
Oil’s surge was fueled by a strongly worded address by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City on Wednesday, where he took aim at the U.S. and President Donald Trump.

Broader crypto prices fell further on Thursday, extending overnight losses as weak risk appetite spurred some profit-taking in the sector.
Optimism over more U.S. regulatory favor– especially after the SEC announced a five-year exemption to blockchain-based stock offerings– sparked outsized gains in altcoins. The SEC’s move helped markets largely look past the failure of the Clarity Act in clearing Congress.
World no.2 crypto Ether fell 2.5% to $2,685.83, while XRP fell 7.5% to $1.5052.
Solana fell 3.3%, Cardano slid 7.1%, while BNB shed 2.5%.

title: Judge blocks Trump’s White House media ban, orders access to be restored
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as surging yields weigh on tech; Trump-Xi meeting eyed
By Jack Queen and Jan Wolfe
Sept 24 (Reuters) - A federal judge ordered US President Donald Trump on Thursday to restore White House access for journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico, saying his ban on the three media outlets was likely unconstitutional.
In a major setback for Trump in one of his biggest battles with the media, US District Judge Tim Kelly issued his order in a lawsuit that the news organizations filed contesting the ban that the Republican president announced on September 18.
Kelly ordered the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets’ press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days. The judge rejected the government’s assertion that the ban was motivated by national security concerns.
"The record lacks factual support for defendants’ contention that the revocation of plaintiffs’ hard passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds," he said, adding that Trump himself had stated the ban was due to "alleged lack of truthfulness and negativity" of the outlets’ reporting.
The White House and representatives for the outlets did not immeidately respond to requests for comment.
Trump had said on social media that the three outlets "shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES," and Justice Department lawyers had sought to justify the ban on national security grounds.
The three outlets sued Trump and other members of his administration in federal court in Washington on Monday, saying the ban violated the US Constitution’s First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. They requested a temporary restraining order that would immediately reinstate their White House access while their legal challenge plays out.
The legal battle has unfolded just weeks before the November 3 midterm elections in which Trump’s fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress. Trump’s job approval ratings are at record lows in opinion polls amid concerns over issues such as the Iran war and inflation.
Kelly said at a Wednesday hearing that two precedents from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit made clear that journalists are entitled to due process before their White House press passes can be revoked. The judge added that it did not appear that the White House had given the targeted news outlets a meaningful opportunity to contest the revocation of their access.
A lawyer for the news outlets told Kelly that they were banned without legally required advance notice or opportunity to contest the decisions, which he said were unprecedented, unreasonable and severe punishments.
A Justice Department lawyer told the judge the Trump administration provided a sufficient explanation for the revocation of the press passes in letters sent to the news outlets on Tuesday. But the judge signaled skepticism of that argument, noting that the letters were sent after the revocation occurred and the lawsuit was filed.
In a legal filing on Tuesday, the Justice Department argued that access to the White House is a privilege, not an entitlement, and that the president has the authority to suspend access by news organizations.
A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations filed a legal brief on Wednesday supporting the three news outlets. They asserted that "stripping journalists and news outlets of their rights because of perceived editorial viewpoint violates decades of Supreme Court jurisprudence."
The brief was signed by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, Reuters, the Washington Post and Fox News, among others.
